Chevron states that its results are most significantly affected by crude oil, natural gas and NGL prices, and that extended periods of low prices or demand have had, and can in the future have, a material adverse impact on its results of operations, financial condition and liquidity. According to the 10-K, upstream earnings, cash flows and capital expenditure programs could be negatively affected, as could production and proved reserves. Upstream assets may also become impaired. Downstream earnings could also suffer because they depend on refined product supply, demand and margins. Chevron says periods of sustained lower commodity prices could result in impairment or write-off of specific assets, and could cause it to adjust operating expenses, including employee reductions, and capital expenditures, along with other measures intended to improve financial performance. Chevron warns that a significant or sustained decline in liquidity could hurt its credit ratings, potentially raise financing costs and reduce access to capital markets. It also says downturns may slow the pace and scale of investment, including in New Energies, and can hurt its suppliers, vendors, partners and equity affiliates. In the Q2 2026 10-Q, Chevron states that for every dollar change in Brent crude prices, its annual after-tax earnings and cash flow sensitivity is approximately $600 million. Brent averaged $92 per barrel in the first half of 2026, so this sensitivity was stated in a high-price period.
